# Judith Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 6

---

## Council Notes

**Key decisions for this chapter:**

- **"Commander-in-chief" vs. "chief general":** LOGOS and PNEUMA favor "commander-in-chief" as cleaner English; EMET preserves the compound "chief-general." SOPHIA adopts "commander-in-chief."
- **v. 2 — "who is god but Nebuchadnezzar":** All three render the blasphemy consistently. SOPHIA preserves lowercase "god" in Holofernes' speech to underscore his contempt for Israel's deity.
- **v. 4 — "drunk with blood":** PNEUMA's "run drunk" is vivid and defensible; all three converge on the image. SOPHIA uses "be made drunk."
- **v. 9 — "let not your face fall":** EMET is most literal (Greek: *mē pipteto to prosōpon sou*). SOPHIA preserves this idiom with a gloss.
- **v. 19 — "those consecrated to you":** LOGOS renders it most precisely. PNEUMA's "those who belong to you" is acceptable but loses the consecration nuance.

---

**6:1** When the commotion around the council had subsided, Holofernes, commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army, addressed Achior and all the Moabites before the whole assembly of the foreign peoples:

**6:2** "Who are you, Achior — you and these Ephraimite hirelings — that you have prophesied among us as you did today, warning us not to make war against the people of Israel because their god will shield them? And who is god but Nebuchadnezzar? He will send his power and wipe them from the face of the earth, and their god cannot save them.

**6:3** We his servants will strike them as one man. No force of theirs can stand against our cavalry.

**6:4** We will overwhelm them. Their mountains will be made drunk with their blood and their plains will be filled with their dead. Not even their footprints will survive before us — they will be utterly destroyed. So declares King Nebuchadnezzar, lord of all the earth. He has spoken, and not one of his words will come to nothing.

**6:5** As for you, Achior, hireling of Ammon, who have spoken these words in your wickedness — you will not see my face again from this day until I take vengeance on this people who came out of Egypt.

**6:6** Then the iron of my army and the spears of my forces will pierce your sides, and you will fall among their dead when I return.

**6:7** My servants will now carry you off into the hill country and place you in one of the mountain towns.

**6:8** You will not perish until you perish with them.

**6:9** And if you truly believe in your heart that they will not be captured, then do not let your face fall. I have spoken, and not one of my words will prove empty."

**6:10** Holofernes ordered his attendants standing ready in his tent to seize Achior, lead him to Bethulia, and hand him over to the Israelites.

**6:11** His servants seized him, brought him outside the camp into the plain, and from the middle of the plain they made their way into the hill country and came to the springs below Bethulia.

**6:12** When the men of the city saw them on the crest of the hill, they took up their weapons, went out to the top of the hill, and every slinger kept them at bay with stones, blocking their ascent.

**6:13** The soldiers slipped beneath the hill, bound Achior, left him at the foot of the hill, and returned to their master.

**6:14** The Israelites came down from their city, found him, untied him, brought him into Bethulia, and placed him before the leaders of their city,

**6:15** who at that time were Uzziah son of Micah of the tribe of Simeon, Chabris son of Gothoniel, and Charmis son of Melchiel.

**6:16** They called together all the elders of the city; all the young men assembled as well, and the women too. They stood Achior in the center of all the people, and Uzziah questioned him about all that had happened.

**6:17** He answered and reported to them all the proceedings of Holofernes' council — every word spoken before the assembly of Assyrian commanders, and every great boast Holofernes had made against the house of Israel.

**6:18** Then the people fell down and worshiped God and cried out:

**6:19** "O Lord God of heaven, behold their arrogance, and have mercy on the humiliation of our people. Look this day with favor upon the faces of those who are consecrated to you."

**6:20** Then they comforted Achior and praised him greatly.

**6:21** Uzziah took him from the assembly to his own house and gave a feast for the elders, and they called upon the God of Israel for help throughout that night.
